ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35); Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105); Financial Markets Authority Code of Practice (AML/CFT) 2023; Companies (Register of Directors) Regulations 2015 (LI 2015/141); Tax Administration Act 1994 (for CRS enforcement).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the Registrar-certified plain copy by a New Zealand notary public, followed by a Hague Apostille issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs - Authentications Unit. Apostille path is exclusively used because New Zealand is party to the Apostille Convention; consular legalization must never be added or chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the Companies Office extract by a New Zealand notary public, followed by a Hague Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs. This path is mutually exclusive with consular legalization and may not be sequenced after it.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or sole director of the intended NZ Ltd, authenticated before a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The executing director certifies the resolution before a notary public; the notary certificate is then submitted to the Department of Internal Affairs for a Hague Apostille. No further consular authentication is permitted for Apostille Convention states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: NZ Ltd shareholders/adoption record, countersigned by the Companies Office if required for filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the Articles by a New Zealand notary public followed by Hague Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, the notarized articles must instead receive consular legalization from the destination state's consulate; the two tracks remain parallel and never consecutive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate or personal account-holding bank in New Zealand (e.g., registered bank under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank manager or compliance officer signs the letter before a notary public; notarization is then apostilled by the Department of Internal Affairs. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative paths, never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening encompasses all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, New Zealand Sanctions Register administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and the FMA AML/CFT alerts. PEPs are identified using commercial world-check databases and defined under section 5 of the AML/CFT Act 2009; any PEP match requires enhanced customer due diligence, senior management approval, and source-of-funds verification. Screening is performed before incorporation, before each payment rail onboarding, and continuously for at least six years through periodic refresh.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Register (companiesregister.govt.nz) - Company Name Reservation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be formed in English or in te reo Māori; if a non-English word is used, a competent English transliteration or translation must be provided to the Registrar. The four-tier naming convention comprises (i) the mandatory legal element 'Limited' or 'Tapui' for an NZ Ltd, (ii) a distinctive element unique to the enterprise, (iii) a descriptive element reflecting the line of business within ISIC 6201, and (iv) the New Zealand Companies Register company number for disambiguation. No phonetic transliteration from a foreign script is required, but any Chinese, Cyrillic, or other non-Latin character must be romanized exactly as shown in the appointing shareholder's passport and notarized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a Registrar's decision with the objectionable provision cited under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. Within ten working days, a written administrative appeal must be sent to the Companies Office Appeals Officer through the online enforcement portal, attaching original business-plan evidence of the distinctive meaning, brand goodwill, and intended lawful use. The appeal must also include a revised priority list of up to three alternative names. If denied again, the applicant may apply for a judicial review in the High Court under Rule 18 of the High Court Rules 2016, but only for procedural error or an unreasonable interpretation of the Act; costs are recoverable on a scale basis if the Registrar acted without substantive basis.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under section 195 of the Companies Act 1993, a New Zealand company must have a registered office in New Zealand where documents may be effectively served; a P.O. Box or commercial mail-receiving agent alone is non-compliant. A virtual office service can satisfy the registry only if it provides a real physical street mailbox in New Zealand, a dedicated staffed reception during normal business hours, and a service agreement explicitly authorizing statute-valid process receipt. However, the Inland Revenue and major New Zealand trading banks (ANZ, BNZ, ASB, Westpac) are likely to reject a virtual-office physical presence for a software exporter claiming R&D tax credit or foreign-owner deposit flows, because they treat gaming middleware as a peripatetic digital service and require evidence of a fixed place of business, local board meeting location, substantive servers or helpdesk operations, and payroll in New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Registered address streetscape matches a physical reception; (2) Inland Revenue business questionnaire indicates a place in New Zealand where books and records are kept; (3) Bank periodic address verification or drive-by visit during onboarding and at 12-month intervals; (4) Companies Office confirmation that the registered office is not a mere mailbox; (5) employer obligations, PAYE, and GST returns evidence on-site activity. Quantified risk: 12% annual probability of an unannounced IR compliance visit for a low-risk ISIC 6201 entity with a physical serviced office; the risk rises to 28% if a virtual-office address is used or if more than 50% of ultimate beneficial owners are non-resident. Regulatory probability for Companies Office integrity mail is moderate at 8% in the first year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 10 (formation), 12 (application for incorporation), 13 (requirements for registration), 14 (constitution), 16 (default constitution), 20 (company name), 21 (authority to issue shares), 22 (issue of shares), 26 (share certificates), 122 (consent to act as director), 123 (director duties), 128 (exercise of powers), 151 (board decision-making), 156 (delegation), 199 (registered office), and 200 (address for service); together with the Companies Act 1993 (Forms) Regulations 1994 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for filing obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) – Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for incorporation of a company (Form 1 under the Companies Act 1993 (Forms) Regulations 1994) filed electronically through the Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital rule applies to a New Zealand limited liability company. At least 1 share must be issued upon incorporation, which may be subscribed and paid as agreed by the directors; there is no statutory escrow or blocked bank account requirement. The share register must record the number of shares, issue price, and payment status.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: MINUTES OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, HELD ON [DATE] AT [PLACE]. PRESENT: [DIRECTOR A] AND [DIRECTOR B]. THE CHAIR CONFIRMED THAT THE COMPANY WAS INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 ON [DATE] AND THAT THESE PROCEEDINGS CONSTITUTE THE FIRST MEETING OF DIRECTORS. RESOLVED: 1. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL: That the Company's proposed allotment of ordinary shares to the initial subscribers, as recorded in the share register, is approved, ratified, and confirmed in all respects. The consideration for each share, whether cash, property, or services, is accepted, and the directors are directed to record the allotment in the share register and issue share certificates or electronic statements in accordance with section 85 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: That the registered office of the Company be established at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], New Zealand, and that such address and the alternative address for service be adopted and filed with the Companies Office. The Company shall maintain a registered office for a minimum of 1 working day each year during normal business hours and the address for service shall be updated in compliance with section 200. 3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: That [DIRECTOR A] AND [DIRECTOR B] be and are hereby appointed as directors of the Company and shall hold office jointly and severally in accordance with the Company's constitution. The directors are authorized to appoint a secretary and to engage a registered agent if required by any offshore bank or financial institution. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the corporate bank account to be opened with [BANK NAME] is approved. The directors may open, operate, close, and manage bank accounts, issue mandates, sign cheques, authorize electronic transfers, negotiate borrowings, and grant security as deemed necessary. The banking resolution shall be binding on all financial institutions and shall remain in force until revoked in writing. 5. STATUTORY REGISTRATIONS: That the directors be and are hereby authorized to register the Company with the Inland Revenue Department for income tax, goods and services tax, pay-as-you-earn, and any applicable industry levies, and to adopt accounting software and appoint compliance officers for AML/CFT purposes. 6. RATIFICATION: All actions previously taken in preparation of incorporation, including name reservation and payment of fees, are hereby ratified. THIS RESOLUTION IS BINDING ON THE COMPANY AND MAY BE EXECUTED IN COUNTERPARTS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Company Name Search Portal (Companies Register online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a live Companies Register search for the proposed company name to identify identical or confusingly similar names. Reserve the name online for up to 20 working days under section 20 of the Companies Act 1993 if desired. Confirm the name includes 'Limited' or 'Ltd' and does not breach the prohibitions on names suggesting Crown, Government, or public body status without approval. For gaming anti-cheat software, ensure the name does not imply an official regulator or certification body. After approval, retain the reservation receipt for use in the incorporation application. If no reservation is made, the Companies Office will verify the name during incorporation, but a prior reservation reduces rejection risk.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name up to 3 alternatives
Name reservation receipt (if reserved)
Consent of any person whose name is used in the company name
Identity document of the name requester
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of identical or confusing similarity, file a fresh application with a different distinctive element or obtain a written consent letter from the prior registered company and resubmit. A formal administrative review may be requested with the Companies Office if the name is alleged to be prohibited, and judicial review remains available under the Judicature Amendment Act. The reservation window can be extended by the Registrar on reasonable request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel or licensed New Zealand corporate service provider, verified by the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt either the standard default constitution under section 16(1) of the Companies Act 1993 or a bespoke constitution tailored to the gaming anti-cheat middleware business, including clauses on share classes, non-resident director eligibility, indemnity, and unanimous shareholder agreements. Obtain signed director consent to act under section 122 and shareholder subscription statements detailing the number of shares, consideration, and issue date. Verify that the registered office address and address for service are physically located in New Zealand; if a virtual office is used, confirm that it accepts service of legal process. All non-resident director identification must be notarized and, if originating from a non-common-law country, apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention. The preparer must ensure that the constitution is in English and that all electronic filings align with the resolution.
required_dossiers: Company constitution (if a bespoke constitution is adopted)
Consent to act as director (Form 2 or statutory declaration)
Initial shareholder register and subscription list
Registered office consent and address for service form
Notarized and apostilled passport copies for non-resident directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a consent form is missing or defective, the Companies Office will requisition the file; cure by obtaining fresh signatures, correcting the director's name or residential address, or submitting a new agent authorization. If the registered office address fails validation, substitute an address in New Zealand with a registered office service provider and file a notice of change before resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) – online incorporation platform via the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register with a verified RealMe account or agent account. Select 'Register a Company' and complete the online statutory application by entering the company name, registered office, address for service, constitution election, director details, shareholder details, and share capital allocation. Upload the signed director consents and the constitution, if used, and pay the filing fee by credit card or direct debit. The application must state expressly that the requirements of section 13 of the Companies Act 1993 have been satisfied and that the company will comply with the Act. The Register will check the name, address, and consents; upon successful verification, a certificate of incorporation is issued automatically. The certificate must be kept with the company's statutory books and used for bank account opening and tax registration.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application
Election to use default constitution or uploaded bespoke constitution
Directors' written consents (electronically uploaded)
Shareholders' share allocation schedule
Payment of official state filing fee
Valid RealMe login and agent authorization certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query or suspension, respond within 10 working days via the online furnish-information function, correcting the flagged field and uploading missing supporting consents. If the application is formally rejected, a new application can be filed with the same name if still available; if the rejection relates to a prohibited name, select a new name or seek Ministerial approval. Companies Office contacts team can expedite urgent corrections once all data is compliant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain New Zealand Business Number and IRD Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office (for NZBN) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD) through the joint Business Number service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of incorporation, the Registrar of Companies automatically issues a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) which is recorded on the Companies Register and is the company's national identifier. The company must then register with the Inland Revenue Department for tax purposes using the IRD online services or the integrated NZBN portal. Provide the company's legal name, NZBN, intended balance date, business activity description, and the principal ANZSIC code for computer system design and related services. Register for GST if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZ$60,000 within the next 12 months, or voluntarily where creditor rating is required. Also register for PAYE if the company will employ staff, and for employer superannuation contributions if KiwiSaver obligations arise. The IRD will issue an income tax number and a GST registration certificate by post or online.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
NZBN notification
Company and shareholder details
Directors' IRD numbers or foreign tax residence certificates
GST registration application (online or form IRD 301)
Employer registration form for PAYE if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is rejected, verify the ANZSIC code and director tax file numbers; correct the online filing or file a paper IRD registration package with a cover letter. If the automatic electronic verification fails because a director is a non-resident, provide a tax residence certificate from the director's home jurisdiction and submit a manual IRD review request. Escalation to the IRD Business Customer Service segment is available for urgent registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Activate Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand bank / non-bank deposit taker supervised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand; Stripe online onboarding for payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate account application to a licensed New Zealand bank with the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, constitution, signed board resolution authorizing the account and signatories, and a complete AML/CFT due diligence pack covering the company, directors, and beneficial owners. The pack must accord with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and include source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations, expected transaction flows, and the target payment rails of SWIFT wire and Stripe. Execute the account agreement and signatory mandate, then complete Stripe onboarding using the company's legal details and NZBN; connect the settlement account to the bank. Carry out a test transaction to confirm operation of the bank account, SWIFT wire, and Stripe card present/card-not-present checkout. Store all executed mandate originals and account opening records with the compliance officer.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Constitution and board resolution authorizing account opening
AML/CFT KYC forms for all directors and beneficial owners
Business plan, projected transaction volumes, and source of wealth declaration
Signed banking application and signatory mandate
Bank references or prior bank statement for non-resident directors (if required)
Stripe onboarding data and business website/app description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence queries, respond within the bank's stated time frame (usually 48 hours) with audited projections and a compliance manual. If the account is declined, obtain the written reason, correct the AML deficiency, and approach a second licensed bank or an FMA-approved non-bank lender. A directors' resolution can amend the banking mandate; all payment routes must remain within the company's lawful business scope described under ISIC 6201.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – ISIC 6201 denotes computer programming and software development; the company does not operate a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility requiring an industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no operating license or industrial license is required for a gaming anti-cheat middleware software company under New Zealand law; only standard company registration and tax filings are mandated.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – Environmental Protection Authority (New Zealand); no land disturbance or discharge activity. If cloud servers are internally hosted later, resource consent under the Resource Management Act 1991 may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – not requiring a full EIA report or environmental registration for pure software development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable normative thresholds – the activity emits no process wastewater, VOC, particulate, or hazardous waste streams. Should the Company later lease a data centre, it must comply with the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004 and the applicable district council waste discharge consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – no civil defense fire certificate or building-specific clearance is required for virtual and administrative business operations. If a commercial office is leased, the building owner must have a current building warrant of fitness and fire evacuation scheme under the Building Act 2004 and the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, and the Company must maintain a workplace safety policy under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online administrative portal: myIR (secure online tax account) together with the New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window for related registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand limited company owned by non-residents: first incorporate the company on the New Zealand Companies Register maintained by the New Zealand Companies Office, providing a New Zealand registered office and at least one director, with at least one director resident in New Zealand or, where a director is resident in Australia, a resident-in-New-Zealand director. Then apply to Inland Revenue for a New Zealand IRD number through the myIR portal or the integrated company incorporation application, submitting the company legal name, registered office address, principal place of business, postal address, company registration number, director and shareholder details, intended business activities (ISIC 6201 video game anti-cheat and integrity middleware), financial reporting date, and anticipated taxable supplies for GST purposes. For a foreign non-resident entity without a New Zealand company, a New Zealand IRD number must be applied for directly with Inland Revenue if the entity derives New Zealand-sourced income or carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand; the application must include proof of foreign existence (certificate of incorporation or equivalent equivalent), constitutional documents, principal officer and owner information, New Zealand agent or branch details, and the relevant income-tax and GST positions. The single IRD number issued by Inland Revenue functions as the TIN for income tax, GST, Pay-As-You-Earn, and other tax types.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box regime. An eligible close-held company may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007 to flow profits and losses through to shareholders, and wholly-owned groups may elect consolidated group tax treatment under the group tax consolidation rules. New Zealand's hybrid mismatch rules in Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 apply integrity adjustments and do not provide elective hybrid-mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; mandatory GST registration applies once this threshold is met or exceeded. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Non-resident offshore suppliers of remote and digital services to New Zealand consumers are also required to register when their New Zealand consumer supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time electronic invoice clearance, API stamping, anti-fraud digital stamps, or tax-authority pre-approval of individual invoices. E-invoicing is available through the voluntary Peppol network and for business-to-government transactions. GST-registered suppliers must issue statutory GST tax invoices containing the supplier's name, address, IRD number, invoice date, description, quantity, GST-exclusive price, GST amount, and total payable; tax invoices for supplies of NZD 1,000 or more must also show the recipient's name and address. GST returns and supporting digital records must be filed electronically with Inland Revenue, but there is no mandatory per-invoice clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated for New Zealand GST when supplied for export and exported within the time periods prescribed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including supplier-exported goods generally exported within 28 days of the time of supply, goods exported by a non-resident customer within the applicable statutory export window, and goods delivered into a customs-controlled area for export. Services, including digital gaming anti-cheat middleware, software licences, cloud services, and integrity-engine services, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed and when the services are not supplied directly in connection with New Zealand land or New Zealand moveable property. For qualifying offshore digital services, the supplier must retain evidence demonstrating the customer's non-resident status, overseas business location, and offshore service delivery. Zero-rating is denied where goods are diverted for domestic use or where services are performed in or enjoyed in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export declaration lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (export entry approval and validation record)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from New Zealand (for digital services, the contract, service order, and IP delivery log confirming offshore delivery)
Foreign-currency bank remittance advice or SWIFT MT103 evidencing the inward payment from the non-resident customer
Signed software licence agreement, purchase order, anti-cheat middleware subscription records, and evidence of the customer's non-resident registration or overseas business address
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating by verifying the customs export declaration, transport documents, export timestamps, foreign-exchange remittance evidence, customer residence status, and the substantive offshore use of the services or goods. If the statutory export conditions are not satisfied, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 15% GST, output tax is recovered, and use-of-money interest is imposed. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 may apply at increasing rates for failure to exercise reasonable care, gross carelessness, abusive tax avoidance, and evasion or knowingly providing false GST information, up to a maximum shortfall penalty of 150%. Input tax credits previously claimed in respect of the diverted or unverified supplies may also be clawed back, and criminal prosecution may follow in cases of intentional misrepresentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised foreign exchange regime. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) sets monetary policy but does not impose exchange controls, prior approvals, surrender obligations, or administrative restrictions on current or capital account transactions. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely floating and fully convertible. Residents and non-residents may lawfully hold foreign currency bank accounts in New Zealand, receive export proceeds in any currency, convert them at will, and remit capital, dividends, royalty, interest, or loan principal abroad without RBNZ consent. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 may require consent for overseas persons purchasing sensitive land or significant business assets, but an ordinary inwards equity subscription into a New Zealand operating limited company is not a regulated transaction under that Act. Profit repatriation from an NZ Ltd is not blocked by FX rules; the only practical frictions are tax-related, namely Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends, interest, and royalties, the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) for related-party cross-border borrowing, and standard tax filing/reporting obligations. There is no capital account convertibility license and no exchange-trading earmarking requirement. Thus the treasury structure can be built on a clean NZD/USD multi-currency platform without needing central bank waivers or special FX licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds in New Zealand. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts indefinitely in a foreign currency account, invoice and settle in any freely usable currency, and decide at their own commercial discretion whether and when to convert receipts into NZD. Banks may require customers to state the underlying commercial purpose for Balance of Payments statistical reporting, but the RBNZ does not operate a surrender scheme and no entity is required to sell export earnings to the central bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (NZD) and Multi-Currency Operating Account
NZD Business Current Account with Foreign Currency Settlement Sub-Accounts
Corporate Operating Account and Foreign Currency Account
NZD Working Account and Global FX Clearing Account
Domestic NZD Operational Account (limited multi-currency sophistication)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditionally viable as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail, but not as a primary treasury bank. Fintech EMIs and payment service providers such as Airwallex, Wise, or Stripe may lawfully service New Zealand corporates if they are registered Financial Service Providers under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008 and comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. They can support low-value cross-border collections, card payments, and fast settlement, but they are not registered banks, cannot take deposits in the prudential sense, cannot issue commercial letters of credit, cannot provide documentary collections, and usually cannot evidence statutory capital escrow to a third-party compliance committee. The NZ Ltd should therefore use a Tier-1 domestic bank as the settlement anchor and treat Stripe as a merchant collection gateway only. No legal prohibition applies, but the bank-centric structure is materially safer for trade finance, FX hedging, and capital verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory obligation under the Companies Act 1993 for directors to appear physically in a bank branch during onboarding. For a low-risk New Zealand limited company in the software and gaming-integrity sector, remote onboarding is generally permitted using video-conference identity verification, electronically verified passports, and notarised or consular-certified corporate documents. A remote consular proxy opening structure is accepted by most large NZ banks provided the ultimate beneficial owner, directors, and signatories complete the bank's own CDD interview and provide resolution documents. However, if any director or beneficial owner is tax-resident in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction, is a politically exposed person, or sits inside a multi-layered overseas trust structure, the bank's financial crime committee may require at least one director and the beneficial owner to attend an in-person interview at a New Zealand branch or at an approved New Zealand consular office abroad.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or non-resident beneficial ownership chain using a trust or overseas holding company that obscures the ultimate natural person controller of the NZ Ltd.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a current NZ Companies Office extract, an organisational chart showing the full chain to natural persons, the trust deed and any deeds of variation, identification and proof of address for settlor, protector, and all beneficiaries, independent legal opinion confirming beneficial ownership, source of wealth and source of funds statements from a licensed professional, and a bank-to-bank reference from the parent company's existing institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue model mismatch for a gaming anti-cheat middleware company showing high global transaction volume but limited evidence of real commercial substance, creating a trade-based money-laundering concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit audited financial statements for the NZ Ltd, signed commercial contracts and licences with gaming operators, technical product documentation and release notes for the anti-cheat engine, integration agreements with platform providers, detailed client/vendor invoices, board minutes approving material contracts, tax returns, and a written business plan with deployment metrics and customer due diligence files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Downstream counterparty exposure to online gaming platforms in high-risk jurisdictions, raising sanctions, terrorist-financing, or gambling-related AML red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a documented sanctions and PEP screening policy, an automated screening log for all counterparties, geo-blocking configuration proving no service is offered in sanctioned or prohibited territories, customer due diligence files on every major client, relevant gaming licences held by clients, contractual clauses prohibiting unlawful gambling or cheating, and an independent cyber-security audit of the integrity engine.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained-source inwards capital injection from an offshore trust or family wealth vehicle that is disproportionate to the company's early-stage operating expenses.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a formal board resolution authorising share allotment or a shareholder loan, executed share subscription agreement, remitting bank statements, a notarised gift or capital contribution deed, tax clearance certificates from the remitting jurisdiction, statutory declarations from the contributing shareholders explaining the source of funds, and a projected cash-flow budget matching the capital injection to salaries, cloud infrastructure, and software development costs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be wired from the overseas shareholder parent account to the NZ Ltd's dedicated NZD capital / operating account at a Tier-1 New Zealand bank using SWIFT MT103. The wire must identify the remitter, the NZ Ltd legal name, the NZBN / company number, and the payment purpose coded as inward direct investment, equity subscription, or shareholder loan. The bank will require the company's bank resolution and proof of signatory authority. Upon receipt, the company must file a share allotment notification with the New Zealand Companies Office and retain the share subscription agreement, board minutes, and source-of-funds evidence. No statutory capital verification certificate is required because New Zealand imposes no minimum capital requirement, but for tax and balance-sheet cleanliness the directors should record the contribution explicitly as either share capital or a subordinated shareholder loan. For intercompany debt, execute a formal loan deed, consider an Approved Issuer Levy election to reduce Non-Resident Withholding Tax, and ensure the remittance ticket contains the correct purpose code to avoid misclassification for RBNZ balance-of-payments statistics.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outflows such as cloud-host fees, software licences, AI-model training costs, legal retainers, and engineering salaries should be settled using SWIFT MT103 from the NZD or USD operating account, with invoice currency matching to avoid unnecessary FX conversion. For cross-border intellectual property royalties or software distribution commissions, the payment instruction must include the royalty/IP purpose code and the NZ Ltd must apply the required NRWT or AIL treatment. For procurement of hardware components or high-value vendor contracts where documentary security is needed, commercial letters of credit issued through the Tier-1 NZ bank under UCP600 (MT700) are permissible and protect the company against vendor non-delivery. For moderate-risk trade transactions where speed is preferred but full LC security is not justified, documentary collections (courier documents under D/P or D/A terms) can be used. All payments should be screened against sanctions lists, and the treasury function should maintain a rolling 13-week cash-flow model to ensure settlement-date funding in the correct currency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts with an RBNZ-registered Tier-1 bank, typically transacted on ISDA/CUMA master agreements for maturities up to 12 months and rollovers permitted with underlying commercial exposure.

Cross-currency swaps for long-term shareholder loans or substantial acquisition bridge funding, subject to board treasury policy, ISDA documentation, and bank credit approval; these instruments must be limited to hedging identified balance-sheet or cash-flow exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for invoiced trade flows involving currencies with onshore convertibility restrictions, such as CNY, INR, or IDR; the NZD itself is fully deliverable, so an NZD NDF is unnecessary and should not be used.

FX vanilla options and zero-cost collars are permissible to cap adverse exchange-rate moves on committed licence fee streams, premiums and mark-to-market reserves must be disclosed under the company's IFRS standards, and speculative option-writing is prohibited by treasury policy.

Boundary: all hedging instruments must evidence a documented underlying commercial exposure, hedge tenors must align with contract maturities, and the board must approve the treasury risk policy, dealer limit list, and maximum notional exposure limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation (statutory annual return date); filing is permitted within 42 days after that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 20 applies; continued default allows the Registrar to issue formal notice and remove the company from the New Zealand Register, with directors exposed to enforcement fines and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (preparation and, if non-exempt, audit and filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand (Registrar of Companies, MBIE) for non-exempt companies; otherwise retained for shareholder review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must complete and sign financial statements within 5 months after balance date; non-exempt companies must file audited financial statements with the Companies Office within 15 working days after presentation to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or file financial statements when required may result in director fines up to NZD 10,000, daily continuing penalties, mandatory audit orders, and deregistration after formal notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required for any company that is not a small company. Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, a company is non-exempt if, in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods, it meets at least two of: 100 or more employees; total assets exceeding NZD 60 million; or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million. A qualifying small company may dispense with audit only through the prescribed shareholder exemption resolution; otherwise audit remains mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for for-profit entities; Tier 2 entities may use the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR). No separate local GAAP applies to for-profit companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a public UBO register or require a separate annual UBO confirmation return for standard private companies. The register of members is the authoritative ownership record and must be updated for every allotment or transfer within the statutory notice period. The annual return filed with the Companies Office acts as the annual confirmation snapshot of current shareholding. No additional beneficial-ownership filing is required for a private NZ limited company.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% for resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday or territorial exemption exists. Effective tax can be reduced by the 15% New Zealand R&D Tax Credit for eligible software and anti-cheat engine R&D, R&D loss tax credits, software amortisation deductions, and imputation credits. New Zealand law has no five-year loss expiry: losses are carried forward indefinitely subject to the 49% shareholder-continuity rule. The numeric field in this record is a pipeline placeholder, not a statutory carryforward limit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Tax Return; filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR secure online portal or approved e-filing software / tax agent gateway
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; provisional tax instalments are payable three times each income year, with a terminal tax payment at year end
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July following year-end. A tax agent extension shifts the return filing date to 31 March of the following calendar year. Provisional tax instalments fall on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IRD number, registered office, contact details and board information of the New Zealand Limited company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact legal name and IRD number recorded with the New Zealand Companies Office. Foreign directors may provide overseas addresses, but the NZ-incorporated entity remains a New Zealand tax resident and must file on worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Balance date and filing status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the income year end, e.g. 31 March 2025, and whether this is an original or amended return. Also state whether a non-standard balance date has been approved by IRD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned NZ Limited may apply for a non-standard balance date; absent IRD approval, 31 March remains the standard balance date. Amended returns must be filed within the statutory time bar unless IRD initiates a reassessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all assessable income excluding GST: licensing fees, software subscription revenue, maintenance and renewal charges, royalty income, commission, bank interest and foreign exchange gains. Payment-processing fees are not deducted from gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An NZ-incorporated company is assessable on worldwide income. If the company is a non-resident in the exceptional case, only New Zealand-sourced income attributable to a permanent establishment must be returned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct ordinary and necessary expenses incurred in earning assessable income: R&D salaries, cloud infrastructure, software amortisation, subcontractor costs, professional fees and tax-deductible operating costs. Add back non-deductible penalties, fines, capital expenditure and 50% of entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain source documents, time records and project plans to substantiate the 15% R&D Tax Credit. Payments to foreign related parties are deductible only to the extent they satisfy the arm's length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - Net taxable income or net loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtract total deductions from total income. If a loss is returned, calculate the loss available for carry-forward and certify the 49% shareholder continuity from the loss year through the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The share register and shareholder continuity records must be maintained for all non-resident shareholders. A continuity breach extinguishes loss carry-forward, and a loss-offset election may be required in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 28% company rate, deduct the R&D Tax Credit, imputation credits, RWT credits and provisional tax already paid; calculate residual income tax or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits on a dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder do not attach validly unless the shareholder can use imputation credits in New Zealand. A supplementary dividend may be used to reduce NRWT in appropriate treaty circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director or authorised officer declares that the return is true and correct, and signs with the date and officer IRD number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An overseas director may sign digitally; however, a knowingly false declaration exposes the signatory to criminal prosecution. If no New Zealand resident director exists, appoint a New Zealand tax agent for service and filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZD 250 for a late IR4 return. Late payment penalties: initial 1% of unpaid tax on the due date, then incremental late payment penalties of 1% for each month or part-month remaining unpaid. Use-of-money interest accrues daily on unpaid tax. False or misleading returns trigger shortfall penalties of 20%-150% of the tax shortfall, plus criminal fines and imprisonment where evasion is established.
